series_level_findings: THE key source is the official history tree https://maratona.sbc.org.br/hist/ (index page lists every year 1996-2025; static HTML, fully fetchable even though the site root is a JS shell). Per-year pages: /hist/<Y>/index.html (1996-2019), /hist/2020/resfinal20.html, /hist/2021/result21.html, /hist/2022-2025/. First-phase pages: /hist/<Y>/primeira-fase (2008-2016), /hist/2017/vagas17.html (+ prim-fase17/reports/), /hist/2018/primfase18.html (+ prim-fase18/score.html), /hist/2019/primfase19/ (reports/ScoreBrasil.html), /hist/2020/primfase20.html (primfase20/reports/ScoreBrasil.html), /hist/2021/primfase21.html (primeira-fase/reportsbr2021/score.html), /hist/2022/primfase22/ (reports/brbr/Score.html), /hist/2023/primfase23/ (contest/Score.html), /hist/2024/primfase24.html (primfase24/reports/Score.html), /hist/2025/primeira-fase25.html (+ subbr-2025/index.html scoreboard), 2026 currently at /resultados.html + /relatorio-icpc-latam-br-fp-2026/ (no /hist/2026/ yet). 2008-2015 have NO national scoreboard, only per-site scoreboards (dozens of links per year, heterogeneous formats: html, pdf, xls, doc, png, jpg) plus the qualifier table; a national BOCA scoreboard exists from 2016 (SB.pdf) onward, and from 2017 the per-site PDFs are named <uf><city>.pdf. The older mirror maratona.ime.usp.br/hist/... has identical paths but is robots-blocked for WebFetch (and WebSearch keeps surfacing it). FORMAT HISTORY: 1996 (UFMG, 'I Consun', 13 teams) and 1997 (IC-Unicamp, 'II Consun', 24 teams from 5 countries) were single-site, single-stage events that WERE the ACM South America regional; the two-phase format (multi-site Primeira Fase + Final Brasileira) started in 2004 ('Por vez primera en Brasil se realizan dos fases de competicion', icpccaribe.org). So brazil-first-phase-1996 and -1997 should be retired/merged into the 1996/1997 South America regional entries. The icpccaribe.org pages (Sudamerica 1996-2003; Brasil 2004-2016; Sudamerica/Sur, /Norte 2008-2016) give a per-year table of first-phase date / #sites / #teams / final host for 2004-2016 and are a good cross-check. CATALOGUE CORRECTIONS: 2008 date should be 2008-09-20 (2008-11-15 is the Final); 2010 date is 2010-09-18 (not 2011-09-17); 2017 date is 2017-09-09 (not 2017-05-31); 2021 date 2021-10-30 (online); 2020 was online on 2020-11-14; 2026 date 2026-08-29. Team counts on the official pages: 2008 360, 2009 410, 2010 432, 2011 536, 2012 545, 2013 586, 2014 643, 2015 639, 2016 779, 2017 816, 2018 746, 2019 726, 2020 799, 2021 534, 2022 556, 2023 726, 2024 880, 2025 1025, 2026 965. Other series assets: Codeforces gyms mirror the Brazilian subregional sets (101473=2013, 101908=2018, 102346=2019, 103960=2022, 104555=2023) and there are Codeforces discussion blogs for 2014 (entry 13749), 2015 (20335), 2016 (47051), 2017 (54535), 2018 (61935); the Maratona SBC YouTube channel streams every first phase since 2020 (2022: tXyFdZgKi7o, 2023: I1NiurdCdi4); X handle @MaratonaProg; Facebook facebook.com/maratona; Flickr user maratonadeprogramacaosbc; the UFMG site maratona.dcc.ufmg.br/info/competicoes-passadas.html has per-site placements 2004-2012; MaratonUSP (ime.usp.br/~maratona, robots-blocked) posts per-year 'subregional-<Y>' write-ups; Carlos Eduardo Ferreira keeps 'Maratona de Programacao USP 1997--2014' at ime.usp.br/~cef/maratona.html (robots-blocked). People: Ricardo Anido (Unicamp, long-time chief judge/director), Claudionor Coelho (1996-97 regional director), Guilherme N. Ramos (UnB, data site gnramos.github.io/maratona-site - currently an empty shell).
